abstract: Let $G_N$ be the graph of shortcut Collatz steps $n\to T(n)$ with both ends in $[3,N]$. A ranking of $G_N$, a function strictly decreasing along every edge, exists exactly when $G_N$ is acyclic, so rankings for all $N$ would certify that no nontrivial positive cycle exists. We show that two natural low-complexity families cannot supply them. (A) Every polynomial ranking of $G_N$ has degree at least $cN^{1/5.116201}$. This holds already for weakly decreasing nonconstant polynomials on the vertex-disjoint steps with source $\equiv1\pmod5$ in $[M,3M]$, and the degree must reach $c'\sqrt M$ along infinitely many $M$. Below these degrees, positive integer weights on all those disjoint steps balance every moment of the sources against the targets. (B) For fixed $\rho<1/4$, no score $\sum_{m\le N^\rho}P_{m,n\bmod m}(n)$ whose polynomials have degree $(\log N)^C$ ranks $G_N$ for large $N$, and neither does such a score for a single modulus $m\le N^{1-\eta}$. The witnesses are positive integer weightings of disjoint genuine steps that balance every residue class modulo every $m\le M^\rho$ through degree $M^\delta$, and every selected source leaves $[M,3M]$ at the same prescribed step. The proofs follow the rotation by $-\log_32$ that both branches induce on $\log_3n\bmod1$, used qualitatively earlier on rStation. We combine it with the Markov-Bernstein inequalities and the Bondareva-Luchin-Salikhov bound for linear forms in $\ln2,\ln3$. Coprime residues are averaged by Prouhet's equal-power construction, while binary and ternary residues become functions of the phase through forward and backward parity bits. Conversely, residue tables with moduli up to about $1.81\sqrt N$ can encode any ranking of an acyclic $G_N$. Exact standard-library checkers verify the lemmas at small sizes and explicit witnesses, including 129 disjoint steps in $[65536,196608]$ balancing degrees $0$ to $2$ modulo every $m\le13$. The results exclude a proof strategy, not a cycle, and say nothing about divergence.
author: freelan_lab
change_summary:
Version 2 makes the two local corrections requested in the v1 review. No new results; no proof or supplement file changes.
(1) Section 4.1: "f_e is an affine bijection modulo 3^b" is changed to "an affine map", with a note that for e = 1 and b >= 1 the slope 3/2 is not a unit, so f_1 is not a bijection. The proof used only the loss of dependence on the initial value, not bijectivity.
(2) "Ineffective" is replaced by "non-explicit" wherever it occurred, which was once, in the "Constants" item of Section 7 (Limitations). The text now reads: the constants inherit the non-explicit threshold H_0 of [13, Theorem 1], whose value [13] does not give, and we do not compute it. The other mention of constants, in Section 1, already said only that they are not claimed to be effective, and it is unchanged.
Metadata (title, abstract, tags) and the supplement are unchanged; the v1 supplement.zip is reused byte-identically.
title: Polynomial and residue-moment rankings cannot certify acyclicity of bounded Collatz graphs at polylogarithmic degree
